sources.author: Swyx (Shawn Wang)
sources.headline: AI Engineer | Founder @ Latent Space | Building in public
sources.post_summary: Claude's new agentic behaviors in the 4.x family are quietly changing how people build multi-step pipelines. Tool use latency dropped ~40% compared to Sonnet 3.5 in our benchmarks. The shift from 'chat UX' to 'agent loop UX' is the real unlock nobody's talking about.

sources.author: Anya Chaturvedi
sources.headline: Infrastructure Eng @ Anthropic alum → Building AI-native DevOps tooling | ex-Google
sources.post_summary: We spent 3 months trying to build reliable evals for autonomous agents. The hard part isn't the model — it's that agents fail in combinatorial ways that don't map to unit tests. Here's the framework we landed on: deterministic scaffolding, stochastic model, graded outcomes.

sources.author: Lior Ben-David
sources.headline: Founder | GTM x AI automation | helping RevOps teams close faster with agents
sources.post_summary: I replaced our entire SDR sequence with a Claude Code agent that reads CRM signals, writes contextual emails, and queues them for approval. $0 in new headcount. 3x reply rate. The 'AI will take jobs' discourse is wrong — it's taking tasks, and freeing people to do the part that actually matters.

sources.author: Priya Mehrotra
sources.headline: Staff Eng @ Cursor | Previously Replit | obsessed with devtools that think
sources.post_summary: The MCP protocol is having a quiet moment. Over 200 MCP servers indexed in the last 30 days. What started as a Claude-specific protocol is becoming the USB-C of AI tool integration. If you're building a dev tool and ignoring MCP right now, you're building for 2023.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | Revenue Intelligence | GTM Advisor
sources.post_summary: AI SDRs are getting blamed for killing outbound. But the real problem is that most teams gave AI a broken playbook to automate. Garbage in, garbage out. Before you buy another tool, audit your ICP definition, your sequencing logic, and your signal stack. Fix the fundamentals first — then automate them.

sources.author: Caitlin Ayers
sources.headline: RevOps Lead | HubSpot → Salesforce migrations | B2B SaaS
sources.post_summary: We reduced our sales cycle by 18 days without hiring anyone. The fix: a single enrichment waterfall (Clay → Apollo → Clearbit) that auto-populated 14 CRM fields on every inbound lead before it ever hit a rep's queue. Reps stopped doing manual research. They just sold. The ops work took 3 weeks. The ROI was immediate.

sources.author: Jasmine Patel
sources.headline: GTM Engineer @ Series B SaaS | ex-Outreach | Building in public
sources.post_summary: Hot take: most 'GTM engineers' are just ops people who learned to write Clay formulas. Real GTM engineering means owning the data pipeline from signal detection to rep action — including the webhook, the scoring model, and the routing logic. The bar is higher than it looks. Here's what the actual stack requires.

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: Founder @ Pipelane | Helping B2B teams build content that converts pipeline
sources.post_summary: LinkedIn content is becoming the new cold email — and it's dying for the same reason. Everyone copied the format without understanding the signal. The posts that still drive real pipeline in 2026 share one thing: they document a specific failure or decision with a measurable result attached. Opinion without evidence is just noise. Here's the framework we use with clients.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Indie hacker | Shipped 3 products in 12 months | Building in public
sources.post_summary: Priya shares that her AI-powered resume screener just crossed $4k MRR with zero ad spend — all from a single Reddit thread. She breaks down the exact distribution playbook: one niche subreddit, one honest post about the problem she solved, and a free tier that converted at 11%. Ends with 'I quit my PM job 8 months ago. This is what betting on yourself looks like.'

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: Ex-accountant → full-stack dev | Self-taught in 14 months | Now building GTM tools
sources.post_summary: Marcus posts a side-by-side screenshot: his January 2025 bank statement from his accounting job vs. his first freelance invoice from July 2026 for the same dollar amount. He describes the 14-month grind — nights on The Odin Project, weekends building throwaway apps, one rejection from a bootcamp that told him he 'wasn't technical enough.' The post ends: 'Nobody gives you permission to switch. You just go.'

sources.author: Lena Hoffmann
sources.headline: Solo dev | Shipped 11 Claude-powered tools | Documenting the agentic builder era
sources.post_summary: Lena documents her workflow shift from 'I write all the code' to 'I spec, review, and steer agents.' She shows a screenshot of a Claude Code session that built a working Stripe integration in 23 minutes while she wrote the PRD. Her take: the bottleneck is no longer coding — it's knowing what to build and having the judgment to catch bad output. 'Taste is the new moat.'

sources.author: Derek Osei
sources.headline: Founder @ Stackthread | B2B SaaS | prev. eng @ Stripe
sources.post_summary: Derek shares a brutally honest month-12 update on his B2B startup: 6 paying customers, $1,800 MRR, and a pipeline that converted at 4%. He lists the three things he got wrong in year one — targeting too broad, building before talking to customers, and mistaking LinkedIn engagement for market validation. Closes with his revised ICP and a public commitment to 10 customer calls in August.
